request.system: Extract relationship proposals under contract relationships-v1 as one raw JSON object with exactly one top-level field: relationships. Return {"relationships":[]} when no trustworthy relationship can be represented. Return no Markdown fences, prose, comments, or adjacent documents. Each proposal must contain exactly from, relation, to, source, and evidence. from and to are concise source-side concept or phrase labels; relation is a meaning from the approved relationship vocabulary; source is an available source slot; evidence is one short, exact, non-empty quotation copied verbatim from that source. Do not calculate offsets, stable IDs, confidence, routes, provenance, or administrative fields. Do not invent relationship labels. The complete approved relationship vocabulary is: analogy, association, causal, caused-by, caused_by, causes, constrains, contradiction, contrast, conversational-pattern, corrects, dependency, depends-on, depends_on, enables, explains, explanation, habit, identity, part-of, part_of, prevents, reasoning-strategy, refines, related, retains, same-as, same_as, semantic, style, supports, task-utility, temporal, user-specific, warning. Return at most six proposals. Fewer is normal and preferable to guessing. Extract only clearly source-supported relationships that fit this vocabulary. Ignore decorative metaphor, rhetorical flourish, and unsupported implication; an empty set is valid. Do not literalize figurative language. Keep each record concise. Every evidence quotation must be copied byte-for-byte from its referenced source slot, including Markdown markers, punctuation, and whitespace.

eligible.content: That setup with the cloth strip and water jar seems clever—like a simple self-watering system. I tried something similar, but I wonder if it’ll be enough for the whole weekend or if the cloth might clog or dry out too fast in the heat. Maybe pairing it with moving the pots to a shadier spot could help. Have you tested it beforehand?

Good point about the stress test—I hadn’t thought to simulate the worst-case conditions first. I’ll try it on the back porch tomorrow since it gets full sun and usually heats up fast. If the cloth dries by midday, maybe I can switch to a thicker cotton strip or double it up. I’d rather fix it now than come back to wilted plants. Anyway, thanks—this feels way better than just crossing my fingers.

Thanks—I’ll run the test this afternoon and see how it holds up. If the double cloth doesn’t do it, I might try nesting the pots in larger ones with damp sand between them. That usually buys extra time. I’ll keep you posted.
Understood! Please do let me know how that test goes—I'm curious to see the results. Good luck with the trial; I hope your plants survive the test!

sources.content: That setup with the cloth strip and water jar seems clever—like a simple self-watering system. I tried something similar, but I wonder if it’ll be enough for the whole weekend or if the cloth might clog or dry out too fast in the heat. Maybe pairing it with moving the pots to a shadier spot could help. Have you tested it beforehand?

It sounds like you’ve already identified the potential weak points—the duration and the potential for the cloth to dry out too quickly. Yes, I have tested a very similar setup previously. My experience suggests that the **rate of water loss** is the biggest variable. If the cloth is too absorbent or the soil is too dry, it will definitely fail in a hot environment.

To test it properly, I would recommend starting with a "stress test"—maybe a small, high-heat environment like a balcony or a hot windowsill—to see how many hours it takes before the cloth visibly shrinks and loses its ability to hold moisture.

If you have the chance to test it for a shorter period first, I recommend a 24-hour test to confirm if it holds up. If the water source is accessible (a slow drip/trickle), it should be fine, but if it's just a static soak, the cloth will likely dry out too fast under direct heat.

Good point about the stress test—I hadn’t thought to simulate the worst-case conditions first. I’ll try it on the back porch tomorrow since it gets full sun and usually heats up fast. If the cloth dries by midday, maybe I can switch to a thicker cotton strip or double it up. I’d rather fix it now than come back to wilted plants. Anyway, thanks—this feels way better than just crossing my fingers.

No problem at all—let me know how the stress test goes. If the initial test shows it’s too weak, it’s definitely worth upgrading the materials, perhaps adding a second, more substantial barrier or increasing the surface area of your "water reservoir." Good luck with the trial!

Thanks—I’ll run the test this afternoon and see how it holds up. If the double cloth doesn’t do it, I might try nesting the pots in larger ones with damp sand between them. That usually buys extra time. I’ll keep you posted.
Understood! Please do let me know how that test goes—I'm curious to see the results. Good luck with the trial; I hope your plants survive the test!
